requirements.text: Native SwiftUI iOS client backed by a real, separately-deployed backend service (not local-only/offline) reachable from the device.
Auth flow with session persistence across force-quit — a fresh account can sign in and returning users resume signed-in state.
Zero-state onboarding never dead-ends: a user with no pod can always create a pod or join one via invite code/link.
Trust-graph/pod membership is enforced as a hard filter on all request read/write operations — no non-member visibility or mutation.
Posting a same-day relay request contains no child PII (no name/photo/face fields).
Post confirmation shows honest delivery-count copy ('Sent to N pod members') based on real push-token/registration status, with a warning when delivery looks uncertain.

Server-side event handling must commit the CAS write and submit the APNs payload within a strict, server-owned bound (target: <=2s happy-path from action receipt). End-to-end device receipt is required to be demonstrated in the two-device demo but is an observed outcome subject to Apple push infrastructure variance, not a hard contractual pass/fail metric.
Data model supports multiple simultaneously-open requests per pod, each independently identified and acceptable.
Accept arbitration uses a genuine server-side compare-and-swap write; polling or client-side arbitration is not used as a stand-in.
Concurrent accepts from two devices resolve deterministically to exactly one confirmed winner and one explicit 'already covered by [name]' loser, sourced from the CAS write result.
No optimistic UI confirmation anywhere: post/accept/release/complete/withdraw all show an explicit awaiting-confirmation state until real backend acknowledgment.
Release ('I can no longer cover this') is available only to the current accepter, reopens the request, and re-notifies the pod within roughly 30 seconds.

A requester-only 'withdrawn' terminal state exists for open/still-open/reopened unclaimed requests, arbitrated via the same CAS path, triggers a re-notify, and never produces an audit/receipt artifact.
'Withdrawn' and 'release' are mutually exclusive by state — only one is ever visible/available to a given user for a given request.
An unfulfilled request shows a visible, numeric elapsed-time 'still open' state with a re-broadcast action, never a static pending label.
Marking a handoff complete produces exactly one immutable audit/receipt object with an internal view and a privacy-filtered shareable projection (no child name/address).
Every outcome-affecting action carries a client-generated idempotent action ID; the server handles duplicates idempotently.
A force-quit mid-accept (after tap, before ack) followed by relaunch reconciles from server truth with no duplicate writes and no false local state.
Same-day cutoffs and elapsed/aging calculations are computed server-side in UTC plus a pod home timezone set at pod creation — no client-local-time logic.
The pod creator can revoke and reissue the join code; the old code is invalidated immediately.
The audit/receipt record persists after either party deletes their account, rendering the departed party as a placeholder.
UI copy explicitly states 'accepted' means a trusted member claimed responsibility, never that arrival/help is guaranteed.
A brand-new pod with no other members shows a distinct empty state/CTA ('share the invite'), separate from 'pod has members but nobody has responded' (re-broadcast/escalate CTA).
Both the post funnel and the accept/resolve/complete funnel implement and can demonstrate all four states: loading, empty, error, success.
No GPS/live location, ETA, or map features anywhere in the app.
No in-app chat/DM thread; only the request card plus one optional short note.
No payments, tipping, or monetary fields anywhere in the app.
No recurring or future-scheduled requests — every request is same-day only.
No persistent scrollable request-history/feed screen beyond individual per-request receipts.
No pod-admin console or member-management UI beyond create-pod-get-code and the one revoke/reissue capability.
No moderation/report/mute/remove tooling in v1; this limitation is stated plainly in onboarding/help copy.
No UI implies identity verification or background-check vetting; any trust indicator is labeled honestly as self-reported/peer-vouched.
Matching/visibility is restricted to pre-established trust-graph/pod membership; there is no open stranger/proximity matching.
The entire build is one native SwiftUI app in a single Xcode project — no portfolio split, no sibling apps.

Distinctive visual design implemented via one tokenized Theme.swift file (type/spacing/color), referenced everywhere with zero hardcoded font/spacing/color literals elsewhere, and full dark-mode semantic coverage verified on every core screen in both appearances.

The free tier includes every core relay action (post/accept/release/complete/withdraw and the resulting receipt) fully and forever for at least one pod; nothing in the state machine is gated behind payment.

The literal two-phone side-by-side acceptance demo passes: two real seeded accounts on two real devices, one shows confirmed and the other shows 'already covered by [name]' within a second or two, zero chat, zero manual reconciliation.

Subscription-tier features (multi-pod membership, exportable/signed receipt history, critical-alert notification bypass) are out of implementation scope for this build — no StoreKit integration, no paywall screen, no gated core behavior; at most an inert, unused entitlement field may exist in the schema.
Mutual-exclusion invariants for withdraw vs release, and pod-membership checks, are enforced as state-machine/server invariants, not merely UI conventions that could be bypassed by direct API calls.
